description.promeva:title: Description (English)
description.narrative: The DRC Joint Response 2020 aims to provide multi-sectoral assistance to respond to the immediate needs and protection risks of the most vulnerable and conflict affected people in targeted Territories within North- and South Kivu in DRC, through an effective and efficient humanitarian response by Dutch NGOs, local partners and actors. The JR partners operate across 6 Territories in North and South Kivu The DRCJR 2020 will aim to provide multi-sectoral assistance and sustainable solution in response to community-identified life-saving needs and protection risks through close collaboration and coordination in the Eastern Zone of DRC. Under the DRCJR, multi-sectoral assistance is understood as an individual or community receiving a humanitarian assistance package of at least three sectors. This requires an increase in developing synergies, strengthening coordination and collaboration in the implementation of humanitarian action. Steps towards increased collaboration were already taken in the DRCJR 2019, in which JR partners jointly implemented their activities at Territory-level. To further increase this collaboration at field level, the JR partners have opted for joint implementation at Health Zone-level. This is based on the assumption that this integrated programming, besides continued sharing of resources (office space and transport) and of technical capacity, contributes to a greater collaborative impact on beneficiaries. The DRCJR 2020 design is based on rapid needs assessments, feedback gathered through the implementation of the DRCJR 2019 and secondary information. The design is therefore based on a number of assumptions, including that interventions respond to the actual needs of the beneficiaries and will have a longer term impact. Another common assumption is that government officials, local authorities and community members will be interested in participating and collaborating on the project and open to increase their capacity. This will be critical for all targeted sectors where the project will work to strengthen the capacity of stakeholders working or contributing to these sectors.

title.narrative: Number of people receiving COVID-19 related assistance (Health)

comment.narrative: A total of 356 people, including 98 women and 258 men composed of 54 health care providers, 162 community relays (RECOs), 120 leaders and local authorities, and 20 health care personnel received capacity building on ICP and COVID-19. In addition, a total of 5,000 posters and leaflets in French and Swahili were distributed in the 18 targeted health facilities.
Covid 19 activities started in July

In the 2 HZs selected (Uvira and Fizi), 18 HFs including 11 in Uvira (HGR Uvira, HG Kasenga, Kimanga, Kalundu Catholique, Kalundu Etat, Kilomoni I, Kilomoni II, Kiyaya, Kaya, Kasenga CEPAC and, Rombe) and 7 in Fizi (CH Mwangaza, Katanga, Kalundja, Kikonde, Mwangaza, Fizi Etat and Umoja) has been equipped with an IPC-WASH stand and received WASH technical assistance to provide essential infection prevention and control (IPC) services, including hygiene / sanitation facilities.

Four local community radio stations (two in Fizi and two in Fizi) have begun broadcasting awareness programs on COVID-19.

title.narrative: Number of people reached with hygiene promotion/awareness raising activities

comment.narrative: Develop IEC material on WASH and key hygiene practice to support community awarness raising. Produce culturally appropriate and context-specific information, education and communication materials in line with identified key hygiene messages.

A rapid needs assessment had been conducted in the 13 locations targeted by the project (5 health facilities and 8 schools) in the Fizi health zone. IEC materials on WASH and key awareness messages on hygiene practices had also been developed. Radio programmes are regularly broadcast on the MUUNGANO community radio and cover all the health areas covered by the project.
